WHERE CATTLE AND BIODIVERSITY THRIVE TOGETHER

Family owned since 1960, Kinloch Farm represents generations of organic practices and shared values in protected open space, land and wildlife conservation, and regenerative farming in Virginia. We seek to enhance the biodiversity found on our farm, and we believe that by farming in harmony with nature, we can help the planet.

SHOP FARM-TO-FORK BEEF
Our Commitment
100% Grassfed Beef

Our cattle spend their entire lives roaming our pastures and are never finished on grain. Our foundation herd have a medium-sized frame which we have selected for our Virginia lands. Our beef is nutritious, lean, and filled with vital minerals and vitamins, including favorable omega-3 and omega-6 ratios, beta-carotene, vitamin E, K2, and CLA.

LEARN MORE
Whole Animal Philosophy

More than just livestock, our cattle play a vital role in regenerating the land as they graze. We honor the lives of the animals by making use of every part– from ribeye steaks to bone broth, and tallow candles to leather bags. We are proud to use every bit of the animal, from “Nose to Tail.”

LEARN MORE
Farming with Nature

Kinloch Farm sits at the intersection of agriculture and conservation, stretching across 3,000 rolling acres of protected farmland in Virginia’s Piedmont. Our animals play a key role in enhancing biodiversity and supporting nature’s ecological cycles. We farm to protect the environment, to produce healthy and nutrient dense food, and to support our community.

About Kinloch Farm

Kinloch Farm spans over 3,000 acres of protected, historic farmland in Virginia’s Piedmont. We operate at the intersection of agriculture and conservation through regenerative and adaptive management across our grasslands, riparian areas, and wetlands.

Regenerative Farming
Our cattle graze on Virginia forages through adaptive grazing that improves soil health, water retention, and carbon storage, verified through research partnerships.

A Sixty-Year Legacy
Founded in 1823 by the Turner family, with subsequent ownerships by the Chrysler and Dancer families, Kinloch Farm grew under the Currier’s ownership to encompass four adjoining properties.

Shipping Orders

We ship all non-perishable orders via UPS from our Farm Store located in The Plains, Virginia. Non-perishable orders can be delivered to the continental United States, Alaska, and Hawaii. Our current shipping days for non-perishable orders are weekly on Wednesday, Thursday, Friday and Saturday.

Perishable orders are shipped on Wednesdays & Thursdays via UPS Ground and must arrive within 1 to 2 business days to ensure quality. Orders with estimated transit times exceeding two business days will not be fulfilled. Our beef is shipped frozen in insulated boxes. Most orders arrive within 1 to 2 business days, depending on location and weather. Once your order is shipped, we recommend checking your tracking information so you can plan to bring your order inside as soon as possible.

We currently ship all of our beef frozen without dry ice, and we recommend that it be opened immediately and transferred to your freezer or refrigerator. If your order arrives damaged, or you have concerns, please contact us within 24 hours of delivery.

Farm Store Pickup

Pick up your order at our Farm Store in The Plains, Virginia. Our farm store is open Thursday through Sunday, from 10 AM to 6 PM.

Beef Shares

Reserve your whole or half beef share in advance. We drop off our animals on the first Monday of each month, and your animal will be ready for pickup about one month after drop off. Quarter Beef Shares and specialty bundles are generally available year-round as inventory allows

Customer Service Hours

We are available via email at sales@kinlochfarm.com
By phone at 540.253.5266, Wednesday through Sunday.

Our Commitment

Our Commitment
100% Grassfed Beef

Our cattle are selected for genetics that have evolved to thrive in our environment, eating grass, native plants, and forbs. Our grassfed beef is naturally nutrient-dense, with a distinctive flavor that reflects the terroir of our region.

Shop Beef

Bulk Buying Guide

Whole Animal Philosophy

As hands-on farmers and long-term land owners, we live in close proximity to our animals. Viewing them as more than just livestock, we follow ethical principles in caring for our cows and hold that thriving and healthy animals perform best within our ecosystem. To that end, we carry the Animal Welfare Approved certification from A Greener World. We honor the lives of our animals by making use of each part, from “nose to tail.”

Nutrient Density

Our beef is filled with important minerals, antioxidants, and vitamins, including high omega-3 to omega-6 ratios, beta-carotene, vitamin E, K2, and CLA. Grassfed beef is known for its anti-inflammatory properties and acids that reduce oxidative stress, which are important for human health and longevity. In partnership with Utah State University’s Food Metabolomics lab, we are measuring the concentration of these minerals, antioxidants and vitamins.

FALL 2024 REPORT
SPRING 2025 REPORT
Certifications
Animal Welfare Approved and Certified Grassfed 

We carry two certifications from A Greener World, Animal Welfare Approved and Certified Grassfed. Each of these certifications audits different aspects of our beef program. Animal Welfare Approved ensures that we’re using the highest standards in animal welfare throughout the lifespan of the lives of our cattle. From conception to abattoir, Animal Welfare Approved audits and monitors the entire process. Certified Grassfed ensures that there is another layer of trust in our products that our cattle consume only grass throughout their entire life and we go about managing our grasslands to complement the nutritional needs of our cattle.

WHOLE ANIMAL UTILIZATION
Whole Animal Philosophy

We follow ethical principles in caring for our cattle, and believe that thriving and healthy animals are integral to our management philosophy. We honor the lives of our cattle by making use of every part– from ribeye steaks to bones, organs, tallow, and hides. We strive to honor the whole animal by transforming overlooked byproducts into useful, lasting goods. It’s an approach rooted in respect, resourcefulness, and the belief that thoughtful farming should produce as little waste as possible.

SHOP PRODUCTS
More Than Premium Cuts

By embracing the whole animal, we’re able to offer a wider variety of products while making the most of the resources required to raise each animal.

Everyday cuts for grilling, roasting, and slow cooking
Bones for nutrient-rich broths and stocks
Organ meats valued by adventurous cooks and nutrient-conscious eaters
Beef tallow for cooking and skincare
Candles made from tallow
Leather goods crafted from our hides

Each product represents another way to honor the animal while reducing waste.

STEWARDSHIP
Our Philosophy
Adaptive Grazing

Our pastures are living laboratories, and we graze our cattle as herd animals would have moved through our region centuries ago. We utilize rapid movements, followed by extended rest and recovery periods to stimulate an abundance of above ground and below ground life in our pastures.

LEARN MORE
Regenerative Agriculture

We manage our cattle in a way that supports important ecological cycles, including the sequestration of carbon and the process of photosynthesis.  By farming with nature, we seek to protect the health of our planet. We take a long-term view, seeking to mitigate climate change, conserve water, and enhance the biodiversity found in of our ecosystem.

LEARN MORE
Ecosystem Restoration

We have ongoing restoration efforts throughout our landscape to restore hundreds of acres of land, that was once degraded and invaded into thriving landscapes that are abundant with native species, pollinators and wildlife. We partner with local research organizations to continue to monitor the outcomes of our restoration efforts.

Philosophy and Mission

Encompassing over 3000 acres of protected and historic farmland in Virginia’s Piedmont, Kinloch Farm operates at the intersection of agriculture and conservation. We believe these two activities are intertwined, which is why we pursue regenerative and adaptive management principles designed to support ecological processes and outcomes across our farm.

Through our management in our grasslands, savannas, riparian areas, and wetlands, we promote native species diversity, wildlife and pollinator habitat, refuge and nesting ground for migratory grassland birds, health and vitality of our waterways, as well as carbon sequestration. We quantify this work through our research partnerships with local, regional, and national organizations.

We pursue adaptive grazing practices with our cattle that are bred to consume Virginia forages and produce an outstanding animal. The grazing herd regenerates our land by improving soil microbiology, increasing water retention, storing carbon, and promoting a diversity of forages in our system. We operate in a system of patience, observation and adaptation.

History

In 1960, Stephen and Audrey Currier purchased Kinloch Farm with the intention of building a family legacy for generations to come. Virginia was familiar to Audrey’s side of the family with Audrey herself attending the Foxcroft School in the 1940s. Founded in 1823 by the Turner family, with subsequent ownerships by the Chrysler and Dancer families, Kinloch Farm grew under the Currier’s ownership to encompass four adjoining properties.  Civic-minded and driven to help improve the economic and racial disparity prevalent in Virginia in the 1960s, Stephen and Audrey were dedicated to social and environmental causes in Virginia, which included their co-purchase of the Bull Run Mountains to create a “green-belt” east of Washington for citizens to enjoy as a protected natural area and a public treasure for years to come. Their primary work was national in scope and they played a foundational role in helping to quietly lead and financially sustain the civil rights movement.

Farming under the Curriers consisted of a traditional Piedmont cow to calf operation, making hay, and growing corn. Following their death in 1967, the second generation took control.  Andrea, Lavinia, and Michael Currier pivoted toward practices that were organic, novel and holistic in scope.  In the late 1970’s the family planted and promoted the first four acres of vinifera grapes in the Piedmont. Under the stewardship of Andrea Currier, in 1984 Kinloch was certified as an organic farm by the Virginia Association of Biological Farmers, and, in that same year, the Leathercoat Restaurant opened as an early form of farm-to-table dining. Kinloch held and managed the National Devon Association records. By supporting and helping rebuild a new livestock exchange, creating a farmer’s market, Archwood Green Barns, and owning and operating an abattoir, Kinloch played an important role in bolstering the development of the agricultural infrastructure of the county.

In the past four decades, Kinloch Farm has grown to reflect the family’s shared values in protected open space, land and wildlife conservation, and regenerative farming. Kinloch’s team of agriculture, conservation, and business professionals form a partnership with the Curriers in order to realize the family’s goal to farm in partnership with nature.

Today, with the interest and convictions of the third generation, Kinloch looks to its future in regenerative agriculture, environmental protection, and community development. As long-term owners of land, we believe that Kinloch has a special role to play in sustaining our region’s food networks, in protecting nature, and helping to steward our lands for generations to come.
